cohort: 252 consecutive women who had a C-section
finding: Skin-to-skin contact with the mother after a Cesarean section was statistically associated with longer duration of breastfeeding compared to skin-to-skin contact with the father or no skin-to-skin contact.
mod_finding: The study found a statistical association between skin-to-skin contact with the mother and exclusive breastfeeding rates on discharge and at three and six months after a Cesarean section.
